newsitem.title: FINLAND: More Finnish banking mergers likely -Hamalainen.
newsitem.headline: More Finnish banking mergers likely -Hamalainen.

text.p: Finnish banks will likely have to merge with each other or with foreign banks, Swedish business daily FinansTidningen on Wednesday quoted Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen as saying.
"Alliances and mergers are likely to increase. Whether this will happen with Finnish, Nordic or European banks, that is impossible to say," Hamalainen said.

"We will probably see larger units but also other institutions which are not clean-cut banks. The advantages of being regionally anchored are today large but will probably diminish along with technology development," she said.

Finnish banks have returned to the black after five years of losses but the market development is weak and competition has increased, and on top of that possible EMU participation will cost banks hundreds of million of markka, the paper said.

"The entire sector faces large investments relating to the technical changes that EMU brings, for instance adjustment to the common currency and the transactions system Target," Hamalainen was quoted as saying.
